characters.summary: Darkseid is the ruler of Apokolips, an immortal New God with superhuman strength, speed and a heated cosmic beam (the Omega Effect) that can disintegrate targets or erase them from existence.

techniques: Omega Beams (curve, disintegrate, can cause a target never to have existed)
Weapons and Apokoliptian military and technology
Teleportation of himself or others through time and space

mechanisms: Immortal New God physiology (but has been killed several times)
Strength enough to break a Green Lantern power ring bare-handed

weaknesses: Radion is toxic to New Gods
Has been defeated by the Quintessence, Superman, Orion, Black Racer, Eclipso and Doomsday
limitations: Rarely fights personally; prefers to manipulate others

sources.supports: Powers and abilities section: strength vs Kryptonians and Justice League, Omega Effect, teleportation, telepathy, radion weakness and list of characters able to defeat him.

feats.claim: Strong enough to break a Green Lantern's power ring with his bare hands; can contend with Kryptonians and Justice League members.

campaignTags.claim: Can teleport himself through time and space.
Can teleport others through time and space.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: flight, healing factor, energy-projection resistance, "The Source" as a weakness, Omega Beams being deflected by mirrors, and a Justice League (New 52) #6 feat. The cited page supports none of them.
No specific head-to-head result with an issue citation is sourced; the page only lists Superman among those able to defeat him.
Durability is not quantified by the source; limits vary across continuities.

characters.summary: In Infinite Frontier, Darkseid is trapped on Earth-Omega, regains his original form by fusing with his alternate-universe counterparts, battles the Justice League Incarnate and is defeated by the Great Hand.

techniques: Omega Beams (inherited from base Darkseid; no variant-specific evidence)

mechanisms: Base Darkseid physiology (inherited); no variant-specific durability is sourced

weaknesses: Was controlled by Pariah and the Great Darkness until freed by Nightwing
characters.formDifferences: Regained his original form by fusing with alternate-universe counterparts on Earth-Omega. The source gives no evidence of enhanced multiversal durability, reality warping or conceptual immunity.

sources.supports: Infinite Frontier section: Earth-Omega, fusion with counterparts, Justice League Incarnate fight, defeat by the Great Hand, control by Pariah and the Great Darkness.

notableResults.note: Defeated by the Great Hand and sent to a place where Pariah and the Great Darkness controlled him.

conditional.dependsOn: Fusing with his alternate-universe counterparts on Earth-Omega

unknowns: Removed unsupported "multiversal durability", "conceptual immunity", "reality warping", "Empty Hand" absorption and flight; none appear in the source.
Powers are inherited from the base form with no variant-specific evidence; owner should confirm scaling.

characters.summary: Deadshot has no superhuman powers but is regarded as the greatest marksman in the DC Universe, with wrist-mounted guns, a sniper rifle and a telescopic sight in his mask.

techniques: Marksmanship that never misses by his own boast
Expertise with all firearms and projectile weapons

mechanisms: No superhuman durability; relies on marksmanship and equipment
Mask with telescopic sight (aim aid, not protection)

limitations: Entirely dependent on conventional weapons and skill

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: no superhuman powers, greatest marksman, telescopic mask sight, wrist guns and sniper rifle, firearms expertise.

feats.claim: Regarded as the greatest marksman in the DC Universe; aim described as near-superhuman.

campaignTags.claim: Wrist-mounted guns and a mask with a telescopic sight.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: a mile-long shot in Suicide Squad #1, tactical body armor, vehicle mobility, a loss to Batman with no issue sourced, and a melee-vulnerability weakness.

characters.summary: Death of the Endless is the personification of the end of life, described as an immortal being of virtual omnipotence, omniscience and omnipresence who can prevent aging and death if she chooses.

techniques: Ending life as the personification of Death
Preventing or granting aging and death at will

mechanisms: Immortal; Death itself rather than an agent of death

weaknesses: Not established; no combat vulnerability is sourced
limitations: Must live out the last day of a random mortal one day each century

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: virtual omnipotence, immortality, ability to prevent aging and death; the one-day-per-century mortal limitation.

feats.claim: Prevented a man from aging and dying by granting his wish never to die.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Death of the Endless, Powers and abilities

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: invulnerability to physical force, reality manipulation, self-teleportation, a cosmic-charter weakness and a "last entity alive" feat (a stated role, not a feat).
Conceptual, near-omnipotent character: combat modelling is outcome-critical and needs manual research and an owner ruling.

characters.summary: Deathstroke (Slade Wilson) is an elite mercenary whose super-soldier serum gives enhanced strength, speed, durability and a healing factor; he is a master of martial arts, swords and firearms.

techniques: Swords, knives and a ballistic staff firing energy bolts

mechanisms: Healing factor (recovered from impalement and brain bullet wounds)

weaknesses: Healing factor is stated to cover only non-fatal injuries, though he has healed severe trauma
limitations: Superhuman but not invulnerable; no ranged or energy powers beyond his weapons

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: serum-granted enhancements, healing factor, toxin resistance, combat training and weapons.

feats.claim: Healed from severe organ trauma including impalement and bullet wounds to the brain.

campaignTags.claim: Healing factor recovers from severe injuries including brain wounds.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: Nth metal armor, a Teen Titans win in New Teen Titans #2, an inconclusive result vs Batman, and a "gadgets" tag (his equipment is weapons).
Right-eye blind spot not verified from the cited page; it differs by continuity.

characters.summary: Godkiller Deathstroke is a Darkseid War-era depiction of Slade Wilson. The cited page does not cover this form, so only his base abilities are recorded.

techniques: Base Deathstroke martial arts, swords and firearms (inherited)

mechanisms: Serum-enhanced durability and healing factor (inherited from base Deathstroke)

characters.formDifferences: Godkiller sword and divine-armor claims could not be verified against the cited source; manual research needed.

sources.supports: Base Deathstroke powers and weapons only; the page does not describe the Godkiller form.

conditional.ability: Ability to wound gods and divine beings

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: Godkiller sword forged by Hephaestus, wounding divine beings, a win over "Gods", and divine-armor durability. The page does not mention them.
Needs manual sourcing from Justice League: Darkseid War material before any variant-specific scaling.

characters.summary: Doctor Fate is a sorcerer empowered by the Lords of Order through the Helmet of Fate, Amulet of Anubis and Cloak of Destiny, with flight, teleportation, precognition and illusion casting.

techniques: Sorcery of the Lords of Order
Precognition via the Helmet of Fate

mechanisms: Amulet of Anubis protection against astral probing and mind control, with soul-trapping and a pocket dimension
Cloak of Destiny invulnerability and protection from fire and chaos magic
Cannot be countered by counter spells due to the rules of magic

weaknesses: Nelson's full powers are inferior to the Spectre's
Nelson's advanced age has reduced his performance over time
limitations: Power level is described as inconsistent across stories

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: artifacts and their protections, flight, teleportation, precognition, illusions, weaknesses and Spectre comparison.

notableResults.citation: Wikipedia: Doctor Fate, Powers and abilities
notableResults.note: Page states Nelson's full powers are inferior to the Spectre's; no specific encounter is sourced.

conditional.ability: Full Lord of Order magical mastery

campaignTags.claim: Described as a sorcerous hero and one of the most powerful magic wielders.
Flight via mystical artifacts such as the Cloak of Destiny.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: a Justice League of America #1 feat, an inconclusive Day of Judgment result, a loss of power when separated from the helmet, and an "Amulet shield" mechanism.
Several incarnations (Nelson, Strauss, Hall, Nassour) differ; the record follows the page generally and is not incarnation-specific.

characters.summary: Doctor Manhattan is a Watchmen-born being with complete control over atomic and subatomic matter, able to teleport, fly, phase, disintegrate people, rebuild his body and perceive past, present and future at once.

mechanisms: Reconstructs his body within seconds after disintegration

weaknesses: Could not erase or permanently kill Eobard Thawne despite his power
Detached from humanity and apathetic toward consequences
limitations: Uses levitation more often than full flight

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: atomic control, teleportation, flight, phasing, force fields, disintegration, time perception, DC Universe timeline alteration and the Thawne limit.

feats.claim: Instantaneously disintegrated fleeing soldiers during the Vietnam War with a thought.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Doctor Manhattan, Powers and abilities

feats.claim: Erased ten years from the DC Universe through time manipulation, leading to the New 52 timeline.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Doctor Manhattan, Powers and abilities

campaignTags.claim: Capable of true flight though he mostly levitates.
Can teleport himself over limitless distances.
Can teleport others over limitless distances.
Can move objects without touching them.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: a Watchmen #4 citation for the disintegration feat, a tachyon-field weakness, "quantum regeneration" as worded, and an inconclusive Superman result.

characters.summary: Dream of the Endless is the ruler of the Dreaming, one of the seven Endless, inconceivably powerful beings; the cited page gives little combat detail and records his death at the hands of the Furies in The Kindly Ones.

techniques: Rule over the Dreaming, a realm mutable at his will

weaknesses: Was killed by the Furies in The Kindly Ones, after which Daniel Hall became the new Dream
limitations: His realm and he himself resist change; narrative note only

conditional.dependsOn: Possession of his Helm, Dreamstone, and Sand
